Proposed Workspace

One shell, two working modes

Workspace: the conversation is the main document. Phone metadata is compressed and Your brief reveals the original message and actions. A single top bar replaces competing navigation rows. History, native search, new conversation, Projects and Routing Center remain reachable.

Focus writing: the same editor moves beside the response on desktop. Each pane scrolls independently; Back to reading reverses the transition. On phone, expansion uses the available writing area and returns without replacing the textarea or losing the selection.

Three real layers: context/tools, readable writing, then real route/usage/Send/Stop. Each layer owns its padding, removing inherited double padding and keeping divider, text and disclaimer contained. The quota/usage functions and provider browser have not been rebuilt.

Honest context

The composer chip and canonical Usage panel both show a conversation-only estimate. The Focus heading labels the draft-text estimate separately. Conversation intelligence explains both, exclusions and any known model allowance. Estimates are not billed tokens; unknown limits remain unknown.

Try in the isolated app

  1. Read the initial phone response, then open Your brief. It reveals the original message, not a second copy.
  2. Select part of a multiline draft. Enter Focus, scroll its editor and desktop response independently, then return: preserve the exact draft and selection.
  3. Use history/search, start a separate conversation and return. Switch Auto/manual/Layout; open usage and Routing Center. The unsent draft must remain.
  4. Toggle Search/Research, attach/remove a file, and use keyboard Enter/Escape. Send/Stop is tested only with an intercepted synthetic request.

Offline screenshots are evidence, not interactive replicas. The guarded local fixture and exact reproduction commands are documented in CONSOLIDATION.md.
